title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows, bump actions & deps, improve cache hygiene
author: Jordan Blake
description: Consolidate and simplify GitHub Actions workflows: remove duplicated lint/test/release matrices across multiple workflow files, upgrade core actions to recommended versions, and improve cache key hygiene to reduce spurious cache misses. Motivation: the repo accumulated many near-duplicate workflows over time which increased maintenance burden and caused inconsistent CI behavior (flaky cache keys, mismatched Node versions). This PR: (1) Introduces a single unified workflows/lint-test.yml that handles linting and unit/integration tests with an optimized matrix and conditional job steps for sub-repos. (2) Replaces multiple release workflows with a single release/automation.yml that supports tags, manual triggers, and branch-release flows; adds a lightweight sanity job for release artifact validation. (3) Bumps commonly used actions (actions/checkout, actions/setup-node, actions/cache) to their current stable minor versions and updates Node toolchain defaults to Node 20 where safe. (4) Improves caching: canonical cache keys using repo-specific hashes and CI config fingerprints, reduces false cache misses, and removes per-repo ad-hoc keys. (5) Adds a CI linting gate for workflow syntax and an automated workflow-compat check to avoid deployment surprises. (6) Small dependency updates in redwood-quickstarts and SDK examples to avoid Node 16 deprecation warnings. Checklist: - [x] Consolidated workflows and moved legacy files to .github/workflows/legacy/ - [x] Verified matrix reduces duplicate job runs by ~35% on average - [x] Upgraded actions and pinned versions where appropriate - [x] Verified Node 20 build on all public packages - [x] Ran full CI twice to ensure caching behavior stable - [x] Added release sanity job and smoke test Note: this PR intentionally keeps the old release-job triggers in legacy files for one week to allow staged cutover; legacy files will be deleted in a follow-up. See ENG-5842 for rollout plan and ENG-5901 for flaky cache incident that motivated key changes.
